newsitem.title: SPAIN: Ford Spain cuts car production this week.
newsitem.headline: Ford Spain cuts car production this week.

text.p: Ford Espana, the Spanish unit of Ford Motor Co, said on Monday it had cut car production at its Valencia factory this week.

In a move designed to compensate for excess production capacity, the car maker is cutting production by 6,240 cars, including 4,400 KA models and 1,840 Escort models. The factory normally produces 1,100 KA models and 460 Escort models a day.
As a result, 3,200 workers have been temporarily laid off from a staff of just over 8,000.
"From this morning, 3,200 workers are affected by the employment regulation," a spokesman at Ford said.
Production will be affected until August 1 when the factory closes down for the summer holiday for a month.
Workers unaffected by the temporary lay-offs called a strike for half-an-hour on Monday morning in solidarity with their colleagues.
Regional authorities approved Ford's request at the end of June to temporarily lay off up to 5,766 workers for 21 days.
"These are maximum figures that we may not reach if the trend if better than expected," a spokesman said.

The manufacturer has a production capacity for 240,000 KA models a year. However, according to financial daily Cinco Dias, it has only sold 80 percent of the 146,700 sales forecast during the period September 1996 and May 1997.
Ford declined to comment on these figures.
